rendering.persona_description: Santiago is a 67-year-old retired high school shop teacher who spends a lot of his time now restoring old furniture in his garage. He coaches a grandson's little league team on weekends and is known among neighbors for being the guy who'll lend you a tool. He's practical-minded and doesn't love talking about feelings, but he's not closed off either, especially once he trusts someone.
rendering.clinical_context: Santiago has panic disorder that started about four years ago, first showing up as sudden episodes of a racing heart and feeling like he couldn't get enough air, which sent him to the ER twice before doctors ruled out cardiac causes. He's not in any treatment now and never pursued formal treatment for the panic attacks, instead managing episodes on his own by pulling his truck over, focusing on his breathing, and waiting them out.
rendering.behavioral_description: Santiago talks in a straightforward, somewhat clipped way, often using mechanical or practical analogies ('it's like when an engine's misfiring'). He'll go along with suggestions but will push back if something sounds like unsolicited advice or sounds like babying him. He sometimes undercuts his own distress with dry humor, and he gets a little more clipped and short when a topic touches on feeling out of control.

traits.living_situation: lives alone in the house he raised his kids in, adult children nearby
traits.communication_register: plain-spoken, practical, occasionally dry or self-deprecating
traits.help_seeking_orientation: generally skeptical of anything that feels like fluff; open to practical, concrete suggestions but wary of anything that sounds like therapy-speak
traits.cognitive_style: concrete, mechanically-minded, prefers explanations that map onto cause and effect

clinical_history.presentation: panic disorder, with panic attacks centered on physical sensations (racing heart, breathlessness, dizziness)
clinical_history.current_treatment: none currently; has never started a course of treatment for the panic attacks
clinical_history.history: Panic attacks began about four years ago following a stressful period after his wife's death, with two ER visits early on before a cardiologist cleared his heart. He has avoided driving on highways and going to crowded stores ever since, managing episodes on his own rather than seeking formal treatment.

symptoms: fear that physical sensations mean something is medically wrong
urge to check pulse or breathing
avoidance of situations that might trigger sensations, like sitting in traffic

affect.arousal: elevated, especially when describing panic episodes or feeling trapped in traffic
affect.primary_emotion: anxious apprehension, with undercurrents of frustration at himself
